product: Centrus Energy Corp. supplies low-enriched uranium, both separative work units and uranium, to utilities; high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) to advanced reactor and national security customers; and technical solutions including DOE HALEU operations plus manufacturing and engineering services.
demand: Management reports healthy demand momentum with consistently constrained supply and strong signals across all end markets. Contingent LEU and HALEU backlog is about 3.0B USD, of which 2.4B USD is definitized, and three new HALEU offtake contracts were signed between 2026-08-05 and 2026-09-17.
pricing_power: Moderate and not yet proven in reported numbers. Average SWU price rose 3 percent year over year in Q2 2026 and management cites upward SWU price pressure from constrained supply, yet SWU volume fell 23 percent and the 900M USD DOE HALEU contract is fixed-price.
competition: Major LEU producers, including foreign competitors that may be less cost sensitive, per company risk factors. Centrus claims its AC100 centrifuge is the only deployment-ready U.S.-origin technology for unobligated enrichment, positioning it against Urenco, Orano and Russian supply.
team: Led by President and CEO Amir Vexler, with investor contact Neal Nagarajan. An 8-K filed 2026-08-18 disclosed an officer departure or appointment effective 2026-08-15 under Item 5.02; that exhibit was not read in detail.
market_strategy: Fund a multi-billion-dollar expansion at Piketon, Ohio for commercial LEU and HALEU plus centrifuge manufacturing at Oak Ridge, Tennessee, using the 900M USD DOE award, customer prepayments and a 500M USD equity and warrant raise rather than debt.
bull: Signed 900M USD DOE HALEU contract 2026-07-01 plus X-energy, Radiant, Antares offtakes; 3.7B USD backlog to 2040; Q2 revenue up 14 percent to 176.1M USD on uranium sales and higher SWU price.
bear: Q2 net income fell 42 percent to 16.8M USD, gross margin down 12.7 points, SWU volume down 23 percent; 500M USD raise at 199.64 dilutive; 90-day analyst target changes net negative (-4 raises vs lowers).
falsifier: First new Oak Ridge centrifuge not completed by 2026-12-31, or DOE FY2027 budget omits HALEU cascade funding, killing about 0.8B USD Technical Solutions backlog.
web_what_changed: 2026-07-01 signed 900M USD DOE HALEU Enrichment contract, 1.07B USD with options, moving from demonstration to commercial; 2026-08-05 Q2 revenue 176.1M USD up 14 percent but net income down 42 percent to 16.8M USD; 2026-08-06 X-energy LEU and HALEU supply deal; 2026-09-09 500M USD stock and warrant offering priced at 199.64; 2026-09-17 Antares HALEU contract. All primary.
web_not_known_yesterday: Not found. No company release, 8-K or exchange notice dated 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-25 was located; the newest event is the 2026-09-17 Antares HALEU supply contract. The investor relations events page shows only the text More events are coming soon, so no newly scheduled dates.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Mix and price, not volume. Q2 2026 revenue rose 21.6M USD to 176.1M USD on 53.4M USD of uranium revenue versus zero a year earlier and a 3 percent higher average SWU price, while SWU volume fell 23 percent. Management cites healthy demand with constrained supply and upward SWU price pressure.
web_suppliers: Centrus depends on third-party suppliers for essential products and services. On 2026-08-05 the CEO said it is locking in a majority of suppliers deemed critical with larger commitments to insulate the project from price fluctuations, implying constrained critical supply. Feedstock and enrichment inputs also carry Russian Suspension Agreement restrictions.
web_customers: Concentrated. LEU segment backlog is about 3.7B USD extending to 2040 and filings state revenue is largely dependent on the largest customers. New HALEU offtakers with prepayments are X-energy on 2026-08-06, Radiant on 2026-09-09 and Antares on 2026-09-17. DOE holds the 900M USD HALEU Enrichment contract.
web_who_loses: Russian LEU suppliers such as TENEX and Rosatom lose Western market share as U.S. enrichment returns; rival Western enrichers Urenco and Orano lose share and pricing power against a returning domestic U.S. supplier. Utilities that relied on imported Russian feed lose a cheap supply option.
web_contradicting_evidence: Q2 2026 net income fell 42 percent to 16.8M USD and gross profit fell 7 percent; SWU volume fell 23 percent and Technical Solutions swung to a 1.7M USD gross loss. The DOE FY2027 proposed budget omits further HALEU cascade funding, about 0.8B USD of backlog. The 2026-09-09 raise was dilutive at 199.64 versus about 147 on 2026-09-24.
web_if_management_right: The first new centrifuge is completed at Oak Ridge by year-end 2026; contracts are finalized with all critical build-out partners; 12 metric tons per year of HALEU plus LEU capacity ramps toward first output by 2029; and the 4.5B USD backlog with 2.4B USD definitized converts as SWU and HALEU prices rise.
web_if_management_wrong: Capital deployment of 350 to 500M USD in 2026 against negative free cash flow forces further dilution. DOE funding and the Piketon lease extension fail, killing the roughly 0.8B USD Technical Solutions backlog, and the contingent, not yet definitized portion of the 3.0B USD commitments never converts, leaving capacity without buyers.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: The U.S. centrifuge manufacturing and construction supply chain, including Geiger Brothers, named construction contractor for the Piketon expansion on 2026-08-05; uranium and UF6 feed suppliers; and advanced reactor developers with their end users, including X-energy with Dow, Amazon and Centrica, Radiant Kaleidos, and Antares defense and space programs.
